formation.title: The Grand Duchy of Tuscany
formation.text:
From the towers of San Gimignano to the marble facades of Florence, the lands of Tuscany are united under a single banner. But the question remains: what kind of state shall this be? The legacy of the Medici offers one path: a patronage state where banking wealth fuels artistic genius and political control flows through cultural supremacy. Florence's palazzi, its academies, its banks would be the instruments of power.

Yet the thriving port of Livorno suggests another destiny. Its free port charter, welcoming merchants of every faith and nation, has created a cosmopolitan trading hub unlike any other in Italy. Open doors and religious tolerance could make Tuscany the commercial heart of the Mediterranean.

The grand duke must choose the soul of the new state.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Florence is the world's greatest patron. Let our banks and artists rule.

modifiers.name: Palazzo dei Medici
modifiers.text: The Medici built their power not through arms but through the ledger and the chisel. From the counting houses of the Via de' Bardi to the workshops of Brunelleschi, Florence proved that wealth directed toward beauty could reshape the world.

options.text: Livorno shows the future. Open our ports to all who would trade.

modifiers.name: Spirit of the Porto Franco
modifiers.text: Livorno's gates stand open to all nations and all faiths. Sephardic Jews, Armenian merchants, English traders, and Greek shipowners mingle in the piazzas of this cosmopolitan port, making Tuscany a crossroads of Mediterranean commerce.

advances.name: Commune Tradition
advances.text: Tuscan city-states governed themselves through elected councils and communal charters long before the age of princes, establishing a tradition of civic participation and republican governance.

advances.name: Arte della Seta
advances.text: The silk guild of Florence, inheriting the craft traditions of Lucca after its sack in 1314, transformed Tuscany into Europe's premier producer of luxury silks.

advances.name: Tuscan Tower Houses
advances.text: The stone tower houses of San Gimignano, Volterra, and Florence served as both aristocratic residences and fortified strongpoints in the factional wars of medieval Tuscany.

advances.name: Pisan Maritime Heritage
advances.text: Before Venice and Genoa eclipsed it, Pisa was among Italy's foremost maritime republics, its galleys dominating the western Mediterranean and its merchants trading from Barcelona to Tunis.

advances.name: Medici Banking
advances.text: The Medici Bank, founded in 1397 by Giovanni di Bicci de' Medici, pioneered double-entry bookkeeping, the letter of exchange, and the holding company, innovations that made Florence the financial capital of Europe.

advances.name: Renaissance Patronage
advances.text: The Medici transformed political wealth into cultural supremacy, commissioning Brunelleschi, Donatello, Botticelli, and Michelangelo to create works that defined the Renaissance.

event.title: The Medici and the Renaissance
event.text:
Under the patronage of Cosimo de' Medici and his grandson Lorenzo il Magnifico, Florence has become the undisputed cultural capital of Europe. Brunelleschi's dome crowns the cathedral, Botticelli's paintings adorn the churches, and Marsilio Ficino translates Plato in the gardens of the Villa Careggi.

This is no mere love of beauty. The Medici understand that artistic patronage is political power made visible. Every fresco, every sculpture, every commissioned manuscript proclaims Florence's supremacy to visiting ambassadors and rival courts alike. The Platonic Academy, the workshops of Verrocchio, the libraries of San Marco: these are the instruments through which Tuscany reshapes how the world thinks.

options.text: Beauty is power, and Florence is its throne.

advances.name: Condottiere Tradition
advances.text: From John Hawkwood's White Company to Giovanni dalle Bande Nere's black-banded infantry, Tuscany stood at the center of Italy's mercenary warfare tradition.

advances.name: Florentine Diplomacy
advances.text: Lorenzo de' Medici's balance-of-power diplomacy maintained peace among the Italian states for decades, earning him the title 'il Magnifico' and establishing Florence as Italy's diplomatic arbiter.

advances.name: Knights of Santo Stefano
advances.text: Founded by Cosimo I in 1561, this crusading naval order operated from Pisa and Portoferraio, its galleys combating Ottoman and Barbary threats across the Mediterranean.

event.title: The Knights of Santo Stefano
event.text:
In 1561, Grand Duke Cosimo I founded the Order of Saint Stephen, a military-religious order headquartered in Pisa's magnificent Palazzo dei Cavalieri. Commanded by the grand duke himself, the knights operate a dedicated galley fleet from Portoferraio on Elba and the growing port of Livorno. Their galleys have already struck against Barbary pirates at the siege of Malta and the Battle of Lepanto.

The order's purpose is clear: to combat Ottoman and Barbary threats in the Mediterranean. But the grand duke must decide the order's emphasis. Should the knights pursue aggressive crusading warfare, raiding the coast of North Africa in the name of Christendom? Or should they focus on disciplined patrol and escort duties, protecting Tuscan merchant shipping from corsair attacks?

options.text: The cross demands offense. Let the knights raid the Barbary coast!

modifiers.name: Crusading Zeal of Santo Stefano
modifiers.text: The Knights of Santo Stefano carry the cross into battle against the Barbary corsairs, their galleys sweeping the sea lanes clean of infidel pirates.

options.text: Our merchants need safe waters. Patrol the trade lanes.

modifiers.name: Mediterranean Patrol
modifiers.text: Rather than pursue holy war, the Knights of Santo Stefano serve as guardians of Tuscan commerce, their patrols ensuring the safe passage of merchant vessels through pirate-infested waters.

advances.name: Livorno Free Port
advances.text: Ferdinando I declared Livorno a free port in the 1590s, welcoming persecuted Sephardic Jews, Armenian merchants, and traders of all faiths, creating the most cosmopolitan city in Italy.

advances.name: Trace Italienne
advances.text: Tuscan military architects pioneered the star fort, with the Fortezza da Basso in Florence and Portoferraio's bastions on Elba representing the cutting edge of Renaissance fortification.

advances.name: Tuscan Printing
advances.text: Florentine printers disseminated humanist and vernacular literature across Europe, making Tuscan Italian the prestige language of scholarship and letters.

advances.name: Grand Ducal State
advances.text: Cosimo I's consolidation of power (absorbing Siena, centralizing administration, establishing ducal courts) transformed the patchwork of Tuscan communes into a modern territorial state.

advances.name: Elba Naval Base
advances.text: Cosimo I purchased Elba from Genoa in 1548 and developed Portoferraio into a fortified naval base, projecting Tuscan power across the Tyrrhenian Sea.

advances.name: Carrara Marble
advances.text: The white marble of Carrara, quarried since Roman times, supplied Michelangelo's David, Bernini's masterworks, and countless Renaissance buildings, making Tuscany the workshop of European architecture.

advances.name: Accademia della Crusca
advances.text: Founded in 1583, the Accademia della Crusca created the first vernacular dictionary, establishing Tuscan as the standard form of the Italian language and a model for linguistic academies across Europe.

advances.name: Leopoldine Code
advances.text: Grand Duke Peter Leopold's criminal code of 1786 was the first in the modern world to abolish the death penalty and torture, making Tuscany a beacon of Enlightenment jurisprudence.

event.title: The Leopoldine Code
event.text:
On November 30, 1786, Grand Duke Peter Leopold promulgated what the world will come to know as the Leopoldine Code: a revolutionary reform of criminal law inspired by Cesare Beccaria's writings on crimes and punishments. Tuscany has become the first sovereign state in the modern world to abolish the death penalty and the use of torture.

The code does not stop at abolition. It reorganizes the entire system of criminal justice: standardizing procedures, requiring public trials, establishing proportional sentencing, and ending the practice of confiscation of criminals' property. The new code reflects an Enlightenment conviction that punishment should reform, not destroy.

Across Europe, philosophers and reformers celebrate Tuscany as a beacon of enlightened governance.

options.text: Justice tempered by reason shall be our legacy.

advances.name: Maremma Drainage
advances.text: The systematic drainage of the malarial Maremma marshlands, begun under the Medici and expanded by the House of Lorraine, transformed vast tracts of swampland into productive farmland.

advances.name: Tuscan Viticulture
advances.text: Tuscan wine estates, the fattorie, perfected the production of Chianti, Vernaccia, and Vino Nobile, making Tuscan wines celebrated across the courts of Europe.

advances.name: Tuscan Risorgimento
advances.text: The Grand Duchy's tradition of enlightened reform and constitutional experimentation made Tuscany fertile ground for the ideas of Italian national awakening.

advances.name: Straw Hat Industry
advances.text: Florentine straw hats became a major export industry in the 18th and 19th centuries, with Tuscan peasant women weaving braids of wheat straw into fashionable headwear sold across Europe.

advances.name: Tuscan Scientific Legacy
advances.text: From Galileo's telescopic observations to Torricelli's barometer and the Accademia del Cimento's experimental method, Tuscany stood at the forefront of the Scientific Revolution.

destiny.name: Tuscan Destiny
destiny.text: The Grand Duchy is forged, but what shall it become? Stability and purpose must guide the new state before it can pursue its ambitions.

event.title: A New Chapter for Tuscany
event.text: The scattered communes and lordships of Tuscany have been welded into a single state. The grand duke's banner flies from every campanile, and the treasuries of Florence, Pisa, and Siena are united at last. But unification is merely the foundation; it is what we build upon it that shall define our legacy. The grand duchy stands at a crossroads of history, and the choices ahead will shape the destiny of our people for centuries to come.

destiny.name: The Conquest of Siena
destiny.text: Cosimo I's absorption of the Republic of Siena in 1559 marked the true unification of Tuscany. Extend Medici dominion over Perugia and Urbino, and raise a Fortezza to hold what is taken, as Cosimo did at Siena.

event.title: Central Italy Secured
event.text: The banners of the grand duchy now fly over Perugia and Urbino. Where once the Papal States and petty lords held sway over the green hills of Umbria and the Marche, Tuscan authority now reigns supreme. The road to Rome lies open, and the ancient dream of Italian unification under a single crown moves closer to reality with each passing year.

options.text: The heart of Italy beats in Florence.

destiny.name: The Keys of Saint Peter
destiny.text: Two Medici sat upon the throne of Saint Peter. Now bring Rome itself under Tuscan rule, fulfilling the dynasty's ultimate ambition to command both temporal and spiritual power in Italy.

event.title: Rome Falls to the Grand Duke
event.text: The Eternal City, seat of popes and caesars alike, now answers to the Grand Duke of Tuscany. Two Medici popes once ruled Christendom from these halls; now the dynasty claims Rome by right of arms rather than conclave. But ruling Rome demands a choice. Shall the grand duke impose Tuscan authority through military occupation and direct control, crushing any remnant of papal independence? Or shall he govern through subtlety, using the city's ancient prestige to legitimize Tuscan power through diplomatic finesse?

options.text: Rome shall know a Tuscan iron fist.

modifiers.name: Iron Fist of the Medici
modifiers.text: Tuscan authority is imposed by force of arms. The grand duke's soldiers garrison every town, and resistance to Medici rule is met with swift retribution. The clergy of the occupied city are not reconciled.

options.text: A velvet glove conceals the true hand of power.

modifiers.name: Velvet Glove
modifiers.text: The grand duke rules through intelligence and intrigue. Florentine spies monitor every court in Italy, and Tuscan diplomats secure favorable treaties through charm and cunning.

destiny.name: Rex Italiae
destiny.text: From the Bay of Naples to the harbour of Genoa, from the towers of Bologna to the hills of Florence, unite the Italian peninsula under the Tuscan crown and claim the ancient title of King of Italy.

event.title: King of Italy
event.text: From the smoking slopes of Vesuvius to the harbours of the Ligurian coast, from the rich plains of Emilia to the marble quarries of home, Italy is united under the Tuscan crown. No Italian state has achieved this since the days of the Roman Republic. The grand duke must now decide the character of this new Italian kingdom. Shall it be forged in iron, a military power that commands respect through the strength of its armies? Or shall it embrace the diverse peoples of the peninsula, ruling through integration and shared prosperity in a true Pax Italica?

options.text: Italy shall be united by the sword, and kept by it.

modifiers.name: Imperial Crown of Italy
modifiers.text: The Tuscan army is the instrument of Italian unity. Hardened by decades of campaigning across the peninsula, its veterans form the backbone of a military power that rivals the great kingdoms of Europe.

options.text: A lasting peace requires consent, not just conquest.

modifiers.name: Pax Italica
modifiers.text: The grand duke rules a united Italy not through fear but through shared prosperity. Subject peoples find their customs respected and their communities integrated into the fabric of the Tuscan state.

destiny.name: The Livornese Miracle
destiny.text: Ferdinando I's free port charter transformed a fishing village into the most cosmopolitan city in Italy. Raise Florence, the seat of the Medici bank, to 46 development and ensure silk flows through Tuscan markets to replicate this miracle across the realm.

conditions.text: Chose Spirit of the Porto Franco
We own Florence and its development is at least 46

Silk is traded in the market

event.title: The Miracle of Livorno
event.text: Tuscany's markets hum with the rustle of silk and the clink of florins. The banking houses of Florence have embraced modern financial instruments, and the looms of Lucca and Prato spin gold from thread. Merchants from across the Mediterranean flock to Tuscan ports, drawn by the promise of fair dealing and open trade. What Ferdinando I began with the Leggi Livornine has blossomed into a commercial revolution.

destiny.name: Emporium of Nations
destiny.text: Livorno's warehouses groan with cloth from Flanders, spices from the Levant, and coral from Sardinia. Build Livorno up from its marsh into a great port and a town of its own, and ensure cloth reaches every market to establish the grand duchy as a trade crossroads.

conditions.text: We own Livorno and it has grown into a town or larger

event.title: Crossroads of Commerce
event.text: The grand duchy has become a true emporium of nations. Tuscan cloth is traded from London to Constantinople, and the warehouses of Livorno overflow with goods from every corner of the known world. The grand duke must now decide the character of this commercial empire. Shall Tuscany invest in warehouses, workshops, and physical infrastructure to handle the flood of trade? Or shall it develop sophisticated financial instruments (banking, insurance, and credit) to manage the growing complexity of Mediterranean commerce?

options.text: Build the warehouses. Let the goods flow through Tuscany.

modifiers.name: Warehouse of Nations
modifiers.text: Tuscan ports overflow with the physical goods of half the world. Warehouses, workshops, and manufactories process raw materials from every corner of the Mediterranean into finished goods for European markets.

options.text: Refine the counting house. Let gold work for us.

modifiers.name: Florentine Counting House
modifiers.text: The banking houses of Florence have perfected the art of making money work. Bills of exchange, maritime insurance, and sophisticated credit instruments keep Tuscan commerce flowing smoothly.

destiny.name: Entrepot of the Mediterranean
destiny.text: Control the sea lanes from Corsica to the Italian coast, build a Dry Dock for the galleys of Santo Stefano, and fill the treasury to bursting. Tuscany shall be the commercial heart of the entire Mediterranean.

event.title: Heart of the Mediterranean
event.text: From the quays of Livorno to the counting houses of Florence, from the Corsican straits to the marble harbours of home, Tuscany commands the commercial arteries of the Mediterranean. Ships of every nation seek Tuscan ports, and the grand duke's customs officers collect duties on half the trade between East and West. The grand duchy must now decide its commercial philosophy. Shall it champion free trade, opening all markets and reducing barriers to build the greatest possible volume of commerce? Or shall it embrace a cosmopolitan vision, investing in the diverse communities that make Tuscan ports unique and turning cultural openness into competitive advantage?

options.text: Free trade enriches all. Lower every barrier.

modifiers.name: Champions of Free Trade
modifiers.text: Tuscany has thrown open its ports to all nations. The grand duke's commitment to unrestricted commerce draws merchants from every corner of the world, and Tuscan ships sail freely through every sea lane.

options.text: Our diversity is our strength. Nurture every community.

modifiers.name: Cosmopolitan Vision
modifiers.text: The grand duchy thrives on the talents of its diverse population. Sephardic financiers, Armenian merchants, Greek sailors, and English factors all contribute to the vibrant tapestry of Tuscan commercial life.

units.name: Bande Nere
units.text: Elite shock infantry descended from Giovanni dalle Bande Nere's famous black-banded companies, known for their aggression and fighting speed.

units.name: Santo Stefano Galley
units.text: Fast, well-armed galleys of the Knights of Santo Stefano, designed for raiding Barbary corsairs and patrolling the Tyrrhenian Sea.

buildings.name: Silk Workshop
buildings.text: A setificio in the Florentine tradition, weaving raw silk and dyestuffs into the finest cloth in Europe.

buildings.name: Casa Torre
buildings.text: A fortified stone tower house in the Tuscan style, serving as both noble residence and defensive strongpoint.

buildings.name: Banco Medici
buildings.text: A branch of the great Florentine banking house, offering deposits, letters of exchange, and loans to merchants and princes alike.

buildings.name: Porto Franco
buildings.text: A free port facility in the Livornese tradition, where merchants of all nations and faiths trade without customs barriers.

buildings.name: Fortezza
buildings.text: A modern trace italienne star fort in the Tuscan style, with angled bastions designed to deflect cannonballs.

buildings.name: Tuscan Naval Arsenal
buildings.text: A fortified shipyard in the tradition of Portoferraio, where the grand ducal fleet is built and maintained.

buildings.name: Carrara Quarry
buildings.text: An extraction site for the legendary white marble of Carrara, prized by sculptors and architects since antiquity.

buildings.name: Fattoria
buildings.text: The farm centre of a Tuscan wine estate. Its sharecroppers tend the vines of the surrounding farms for half the harvest, and its steward keeps the cellar. Since Cosimo III drew the bounds of Chianti in 1716, the estates inside them have planted and pruned for a name, and the vintage is larger for it.

where.text: The location's raw material is Wine

buildings.name: Cappelleria
buildings.text: A workshop producing the celebrated Florentine straw hats, woven from locally grown wheat straw and dyed in fashionable colors.

buildings.name: Osservatorio
buildings.text: An astronomical observatory and scientific academy in the tradition of Galileo, equipped with telescopes and instruments for natural philosophy.

buildings.name: Palazzo Ducale
buildings.text: The grand ducal palace, seat of Medici power, where the destiny of Italy is decided in marble halls adorned with the finest art of the Renaissance.

buildings.name: Fondaco
buildings.text: An international trade warehouse and exchange in the Venetian tradition, where merchants of all nations store goods, negotiate contracts, and settle accounts.

list.name: Signoria delle Arti
list.text: The executive priors of the Florentine commune, drawn by lot from the major and minor guilds for two-month terms. The 1293 Ordinamenti di Giustizia of Giano della Bella formalised the Signoria of nine and barred the magnati clans from holding office. Through Albizzi and Medici regimes the institution survived until Alessandro de' Medici was made hereditary duke in 1532, defining Florentine republican identity for two and a half centuries.

list.name: Otto di Guardia e Balia
list.text: Florence's permanent magistracy of public security, founded 2 September 1378 after the Ciompi revolt and made permanent on 21 January 1380. Eight citizens drawn from the guilds prosecuted political crime, theft, and disorder across Florence and its contado from the Palazzo del Podesta. After 1537 Cosimo I transformed it into the central criminal court of the Grand Duchy and the principal instrument of Medici control over Tuscany.

list.name: Magistrato dei Pupilli
list.text: The Officials of Wards and Adults, established 30 July 1393 to take over from the Officials of the Monte the protection of orphans whose fathers had died intestate, of widows, and of adults with mental or physical disabilities. The magistracy administered estates, executed wills, and judged civil and criminal cases involving its wards. Continuous from the Republic through the Principato and into the Lorraine reforms, it was a distinctively civic Florentine institution.

list.name: Monte Comune
list.text: The Florentine consolidated public debt, founded in 1343 by merging the prestanze (forced loans) into a single fund paying five percent in transferable luoghi. It was the first true public debt in Christian Europe and the financial engine of the Republic's wars. The Monte delle Doti, added in 1425, allowed fathers to deposit dowries for unborn daughters at compound interest, redeemable on marriage. Together the Monti tied the fortunes of Florentine families to the solvency of the commune.

list.name: Banco Mediceo
list.text: The Medici Bank, founded by Giovanni di Bicci on 1 October 1397 and brought to its zenith by Cosimo il Vecchio between 1429 and 1464. At its peak it ran branches in Rome, Venice, Geneva, Lyon, Bruges, London, Avignon, Pisa, and Milan, served as principal banker to the papacy, and underwrote the wool and silk industries. Its collapse under Lorenzo's mismanagement in 1494 weakened the dynasty, but the Tuscan financial network it built persisted as the template for the Grand Ducal banking apparatus.

list.name: Tribunale di Mercanzia
list.text: The commercial tribunal of Florence, established in 1308 to arbitrate disputes between members of the five major guilds and between Florentines and foreign merchants. Its judges, drawn from the Arti, applied merchant custom (the lex mercatoria) over civil law in matters of insurance, partnership, bankruptcy, and bills of exchange. The Mercanzia's Universita gave Florentine commerce the legal predictability that made the Banco Mediceo and the Tuscan textile trades possible across Latin Christendom.

list.name: Studio di Pisa
list.text: The Tuscan university. Boniface VIII's bull of 3 September 1343 chartered the Studium Generale of Pisa, and Lorenzo de' Medici refounded it on 1 November 1473 by transferring most faculties from the Studio Fiorentino, deliberately consolidating Tuscan higher learning in a single seat. Galileo held the chair of mathematics from 1589 to 1592, and Cosimo II appointed him court philosopher in 1610; the Studio's law and medical faculties shaped a generation of Italian jurists and physicians.
